routes.name: LiAlH4 reduction of phenylacetic acid to 2-phenylethanol
routes.rationale: Direct single-disconnection route: reduce phenylacetic acid (2-phenylethanoic acid, O=C(O)Cc1ccccc1) with lithium aluminum hydride to the corresponding primary alcohol 2-phenylethanol (OCCc1ccccc1). Carboxylic acids are quantitatively reduced to primary alcohols by LiAlH4 via the aluminate carboxylate, aldehyde-level intermediate and aluminum alkoxide, released on aqueous workup. This is a standard, high-yielding transformation for arylacetic acids in general synthetic practice; no retrieved record documents this exact substrate conversion, so the route is proposed on general reaction knowledge with that limitation disclosed. Phenylacetic acid is a simple, widely used commodity leaf; its stock membership is unverified. One reaction, depth 1, within max_depth 3 and max_total_reactions 3.

Carboxylic-acid reduction consumes one hydride equivalent on the acidic proton, so excess LiAlH4 is required; stoichiometry is not optimized here.
Aqueous acidic workup is required to liberate the alcohol from aluminum alkoxide salts and is not represented as a separate reaction.
LiAlH4 moisture sensitivity limits reagent handling; no conditions, yields, or scale are claimed.

The substrate contains no reducible aryl or benzylic C-H bonds at risk under these conditions, but over-reduction is not a concern here; the main risk is procedural, not chemoselectivity.

routes.name: Asymmetric transfer hydrogenation of acetophenone to (R)-1-phenylethanol
routes.rationale: The only stereogenic element of the target is the benzylic secondary alcohol carbon. The most direct disconnection is reduction of the corresponding prochiral ketone, acetophenone (CC(=O)c1ccccc1), in a single enantioselective step. Asymmetric transfer hydrogenation of ketones with Noyori-type chiral (arene)Ru-TsDPEN complexes is an established method class (retrieved records epmc:MED:32463162, epmc:MED:25853228, and transfer hydrogenation with >90% ee in epmc:MED:31314486), using a hydrogen donor such as 2-propanol; the aryl methyl ketone pattern of acetophenone is the archetypal substrate class for this method, and one C=O reduction forms the C-O stereocentre with no additional functional-group manipulation required.
feasibility_risks: No exact-substrate precedent for acetophenone in the retrieved records; selectivity transfer from other ketone substrates is not assured.
Catalyst enantiomer that affords the R configuration on acetophenone is not established by the retrieved sources; wrong enantiomer selection would give the S alcohol.
Hydrogen donor identity and conditions (solvent, temperature, base) are not specified in retrieved sources.
Starting-material and catalyst availability unverified (inventory unknown).
Chemical feasibility of this specific reduction is not established by validation or by the cited abstracts.

controls.control: The R benzylic stereocentre is created de novo by enantioselective transfer hydrogenation of prochiral acetophenone with a chiral Noyori-type [(arene)Ru(TsDPEN)Cl] precatalyst and 2-propanol as hydrogen donor: one enantiomer of the TsDPEN ligand delivers hydride to one face of the ketone, giving the R alcohol. The retrieved records establish this catalyst class reduces aryl/sulfone ketones enantioselectively but do not state which catalyst enantiomer gives R for acetophenone; the ligand-enantiomer-to-product-configuration mapping is therefore unresolved and must be confirmed (opposite ligand enantiomer gives the S alcohol). No chiral-pool input is required; the stereocentre is entirely catalyst-controlled.
risks: Analogue evidence only: enantioselectivities reported for other ketone substrates must not be transferred to acetophenone.
Catalyst enantiomer required for R configuration on acetophenone is not documented in retrieved sources.
CIP label correspondence between catalyst handedness and product configuration is not predictable from retrieved text.
Background non-enantioselective reduction (e.g. by donor solvent) could erode ee.
